sections.html:
Post Falls is a Kootenai County city on the Rathdrum Prairie, right at the Washington border and about 20 miles east of Spokane. Coeur d'Alene adjoins it on the east and the Spokane River forms its southern edge. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 46,715 residents, up 21.0 percent from 38,620 in April 2020.

Prices run high for Idaho. Owner-occupied units had a median value of $477,400 in the 2020 to 2024 survey, and median household income is $82,183. About 64.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied, median gross rent is $1,469, and about 87 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. People who move here tend to stay.

A citywide median says little about a single house. Many Post Falls houses are worth enough that listing is the better route when the home is in good repair, and that is a fair choice.

Post Falls has four distinct seasons and plenty of snow. A typical year brings about 59.3 inches of snowfall and 25.73 inches of total precipitation, and December and January are the snowiest months at about 17 to 19 inches each. Records run from minus 30 degrees to 109.

  • Roofs carry snow for months, so buyers look at the age and slope of yours.
  • Gutters, downspouts and drainage matter at spring thaw, when snowmelt can reach crawl spaces.
  • Heating systems and insulation draw questions in a city with this much snow.

If you have put off any of that work, an as-is sale lets the buyer take it on instead of you paying before you list.

Interstate 90 runs through the city, linking Spokane on the west with Coeur d'Alene on the east. Idaho 41 meets the interstate east of town and runs 8 miles north to Rathdrum, and US 95 lies about 7 miles east. Spokane International Airport handles air travel. The mean commute is 24.1 minutes.

Public schools belong to the Post Falls School District 273, including Post Falls Middle School and the elementary schools Greensferry, Mullan Trail, Ponderosa, Prairie View, Seltice, Treaty Rock and West Ridge, plus Frederick Post Kindergarten. Private choices include Classical Christian Academy and Genesis Prep Academy.

Buyers with children often ask which elementary school feeds a given address. Have the district's boundary information at hand if you can.

Under Idaho Code section 63-903, all property taxes are due in full on December 20 of the year they are levied, though owners of real property may pay in two halves. The second half is due June 20.

WhenWhat happens in Kootenai County
End of MayAssessment notices go out
Fourth Monday of JuneBoard of Equalization appeal deadline
June 20Second half due
First week of DecemberTax bills arrive
December 20Full payment or first half due

About 45 taxing districts plus several special districts share in your bill.

• Pay by mail only with a USPS postmark on or before the due date, since only those payments count as on time.
  • If you cannot pay, you may apply to the Board of County Commissioners for financial hardship relief at (208) 446-1600.
  • When real property is three years delinquent, the parcel enters the tax deed process, and the owner must pay the third year in full to stop it.

The tax deed rule matters most for sellers who have fallen behind. If that is you, say so when you ask for an offer, because the closing date and payoff need to be planned around it. The Kootenai County Treasurer's FAQ and property tax process page cover the details.

The City of Post Falls issues building permits for construction and renovation, and its Building page explains the process and codes. A change of use or occupancy needs its own permit, which matters if a house was ever used as an office or a rental.

The state's disclosure rule applies on top of that. Idaho Code section 55-2501 and the sections after it require sellers of residential property with one to four units to complete a property condition disclosure form, and section 55-2508 gives the standard form. Describe known problems in plain terms, including anything done without a permit.

Sorting your records first makes any sale go smoother, and it matters more here because of how much snow and weather work the houses endure. Pull together these items:

  • The latest tax bill from Kootenai County, plus proof of what you have paid this year.
  • Any permit paperwork, including for a change of use such as an office or rental.
  • Dates and receipts for roof, furnace and foundation work.
  • Your notes for the disclosure form, written in plain terms.
  • Payoff details for any mortgage.

Hand the same folder to a listing agent or a cash buyer and you will get better answers from either one.

Heirs often live in another town and have never seen the roof or the furnace. If that describes you, a cash sale removes the need to travel back for repairs, cleanouts and showings. The house is bought as it stands, and the title company handles the paperwork and pays any balance owed from the proceeds.

Check the county tax record early. Unpaid taxes can pile up on a vacant property, and three years of delinquency starts the tax deed process described above. Knowing where the account stands lets you set a closing date with room to spare.

sections.h2: When a cash sale makes sense
sections.html:
Time or condition is the usual reason. Top price is not.

  • You inherited a house in Kootenai County and live elsewhere.
  • The house needs a roof, a furnace or foundation work that you cannot fund.
  • You are behind on taxes or a mortgage and need to close on a set date.

We buy as-is, and you do not clean, repair or stage. We make an offer after we learn about the house, and you owe nothing if you decline. We do not promise a price before we see the property.

The steps run in order. You describe the house and any money owed on it, we make an offer, and if you accept a title company closes the sale, pays off the mortgage or unpaid taxes from the proceeds and pays you the remainder. Bring your latest tax bill, any permit records and notes on the roof, furnace and foundation to speed it up.

faqs.q: When are Kootenai County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due in full on December 20 under Idaho Code 63-903, and owners of real property may pay in two halves. The second half is due June 20.

faqs.q: What happens if I fall three years behind on Post Falls property taxes?
faqs.a: The parcel enters the tax deed process. The owner must pay the third year in full to stop it, or the property can be deeded to Kootenai County.

faqs.q: Which school district is Post Falls in?
faqs.a: The Post Falls School District 273 serves the city. Confirm the boundary for your address with the district.

faqs.q: Do I need to repair my Post Falls house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. We buy as-is, so snow damaged roofs, old furnaces and cosmetic wear can stay as they are. You still complete the Idaho property condition disclosure form.

faqs.q: How much snow does Post Falls get?
faqs.a: About 59.3 inches in a typical year, with December and January the snowiest months. Total precipitation averages about 25.7 inches.
